text: Twenty-two seconds left on the enrage. The Bell-Ringer rings without stopping, ring after ring, and the dome is coming down around them.
A slab the size of a car falls. Jaeha calls Borro back into field form, five fresh minutes, and Borro lifts his shield over everyone.
Its weight lands in Jaeha. One hundred and twenty percent. Overload.
The slab shatters, and the rubble buries Borro to the waist. The shield stays up.
He can hold this, he says calmly. But he can't walk anymore.
Nib has forty seconds of field form left, his knives are notched, and he can't cut that bell.
Mok grabs Jaeha's vest in a panic. The trap rat always has a trick. Do something!
At the edge of Jaeha's vision, the held call pulses.
Jaeha's face goes cold. He does have one, sir. He's been saving it for Mok.
For ten seconds, Jaeha won't be able to move, so Mok has to keep him alive. Mok can't believe it. Him?
Yerin nods hard, hands glowing. Go. They've got him.
With a bloody fingertip, Jaeha touches the tiny mark, and it blooms open.
The Call: endless black water, and this time only one rift, a wide river under a silver sky. One minute to make his offer.
Jaeha faces it, bleeding, silver light on his face.
A woman's laugh carries over the water. She remembers him: well, well, the merchant with the free ramen.
Jaeha winces. He's improved since then. His offers have, anyway.
On a boulder by the river sits a tall woman with a long beaded braid and a white bow across her knees.
She glances back with one river-blue eye. Then impress her. He's bleeding all over her river.
In the corner of the Call, the enrage timer keeps running. Seventeen seconds.
So Jaeha gets to it. What does she want? Fast. His friends have seventeen seconds.
She counts on her fingers. One, applause, lots of it. Two, money, also lots.
Then the smile fades. Three. Her little brother, Ilan, left their river. Find him.
Far off, an empty boat is tied to a stilt house. Nobody's there.
He can't promise he'll find him. He can promise he'll look, and never stop. And whatever hits her, he'll carry half.
Pretty words, she says. And the applause? The money?
The timer: twelve seconds left.
Jaeha grins through the blood and points back at the world. Six hundred thousand people are watching. Make it a good entrance.
Her eyes go huge and sparkling. Six hundred thousand?
She leaps straight at the rift. Stand back, merchant!
Accepted, with nine seconds to spare on the call. Summon number three is coming through. All three slots are full, and Route Alignment drops back to zero.
Back in the chamber, Jaeha's eyes snap open, and a cyan slit tears open beside the giant's head.
And she makes an entrance: landing on the giant's shoulder in a spray of river water, bow at full draw, silver braid flying, like the whole chamber is her stage.
Under the shield, Jaeha goes bright red and looks anywhere else. Nib stares, unimpressed.
Bomi's stream jumps to eight hundred and seventy thousand, and the chat explodes. A third one?
Out in the nave, Sora's compass needle spins wildly round and round, blazing violet.
She laughs out loud. Three. Director Baek is going to love him.
Lyra, river archer of the Far Side, summon number three. Her first question: which one is the camera? She wants her good side.
In the drone's lens, a tiny Lyra strikes a pose and winks.
Jaeha shouts up at her. The crack in the bell. Nine seconds!
Then the performance stops. Her eyes go cold and still, and she aims point-blank at the crack.
Her arrow streaks straight at it,
and bounces off the bronze with a spark, leaving barely a scratch.
Lyra stares after it, outraged.
And Nib's field form runs out. He drops to one knee, with a minute of cooldown ahead.
The giant swats at its own shoulder, and Lyra flips clear.
She lands on the rim of Borro's shield.
Everyone stands on his shield today, Borro sighs. Then be a good shield, she says, and hold still.
Seven seconds. Jaeha's eyes move from Borro's shield to Lyra crouched on top of it.
He remembers the aqueduct: Nib on Borro's shield, the force running up into him.
Her arrows are too light. So give them weight.
One hand on Borro's shell, the other reaching for Lyra's boot. Don't shoot until he says. Wait for its next blow.
She's been here six seconds, and he's already giving her orders?
The giant snatches up its clapper and raises it high over their pillar.
And Mok, without being asked, raises his cracked shield beside Borro's. Shut up. He's a tank. It's what he does.
For a moment, Jaeha just stares at Mok's shield.
Lyra draws to her cheek. Count the arrows if you want. She only needs the one.
Only three arrows left in her quiver.
Under Jaeha's trembling palm, flat on Borro's shell, white-gold light gathers.
His other hand reaches up, fingertips almost touching her heel.
The clapper comes down at the two shields. Lyra crouches at full draw.
The red window: three seconds.
Lyra's eye runs down the shaft to the crack, cold and still.
And Jaeha waits for the blow. Not yet. Not yet...
